title: C#/XAML Dependency Graph compatibility verdict
description: The per-repository answer to 'can this repository be analysed at all', decided from structure alone before any convention is gathered. A verdict reads the repository and writes nothing in it. `compatible` means profile work proceeds. `incompatible` means the person is told which structures cannot be handled and is offered a new specification. `unknown` means the structure could not be read at all, and profile work proceeds as it does today with one note saying so.

repository.description: The slug of the repository the verdict is about: the folder name through the same slug rule the validation records use, so it matches that checkout's expected-answer record.

verdict.description: Which answer this repository gets. `incompatible` must carry at least one reason, because a refusal that names nothing is the generic failure this verdict exists to replace.

reasons.description: Every failed observation, in a stable order. Empty for `compatible`. One note for `unknown`.

analysisFileCap.description: The number of files the analysis will read before it stops. The same constant stops the analysis, so a repository counted above it cannot be read in full.

facts.title: StructureFacts
facts.description: What one path walk saw. Counts are of files under the built-in selection, which is the selection the analysis would use with no profile present. No file is opened to produce these.

projectFiles.description: Repository-relative paths ending `.csproj`, `.fsproj`, `.vbproj` or `.vcxproj`, sorted. A project file is recorded as a fact and never decides the verdict on its own.

truncated.description: True when the walk stopped at the cap, so the two counts are a floor rather than a total.

code.description: Which observation failed. `no-csharp` and `no-xaml` are the two languages the analysis reads; `over-analysis-cap` is a repository larger than the analysis will read; `unsupported-project` is a project kind the analysis does not read at all.

structure.description: The thing that cannot be handled, in the reader's words: `no C# files`, or a repository-relative project path such as `src/Other.fsproj`.

message.description: One plain sentence naming the counts where the counts are the evidence. It is shown to the person and reused verbatim in the update request.

evidence.description: Counts and up to three repository-relative paths that justify the reason. Never empty: a reason with no evidence is an opinion. No absolute path, machine name or timestamp, so the verdict stays portable.
